tags: Merge route: a commit names its card, and a merge needs the card finished
git Pull Request: Merge route: a commit names its card, and a merge needs the card finished
events.content:
The authorship half of the merge route had one part: a verdict signed by a different npub. The
other two are what make "who wrote this, and may it land" answerable from the tree itself rather
than only from the board.

- `scripts/card_trailer.sh` is a `commit-msg` hook, installed once per clone exactly like the
  push guard. A card workspace writes `Card: t_xxxxxxxx` (the dispatcher's marker, or the id at
  the front of the `.worktrees/` path); the operator's checkout writes `Card: operator`, so
  operator work says so instead of saying nothing. A message that already carries a trailer is
  left alone, so an operator working for a card writes the id themselves. Hooks live in the
  shared git directory, so one install covers every card the dispatcher creates afterwards, and
  `status` says whether the installed copy has drifted from the script.

- `scripts/merge_pr.sh` refuses (exit 6) a PR any of whose commits carries no `Card:` trailer,
  and names them. It is checked there and never written there: a merge-time attribution would
  be a guess for a PR whose commits never said, and rewriting them would change the history the
  review covered. `git log` therefore answers "which card wrote this line" without the board,
  and because an ngit PR's description is built from its commits' messages, the PR says it too.

- `ngit_merge.py` is the board's half: the merge route refuses (exit 7) a PR whose card is not
  in `review` or `done`, naming the card and the status it actually has. The card comes from
  the bridge's `ngit_links` row for the PR root and from every card the trailers name, so
  `Card: operator` cannot release a card the bridge linked. When the bridge has not linked the
  PR yet the board comes from the checkout's `concord.projects` entry, so a block of operator
  work under a card is still checked rather than skipped. `hng ngit merge-check <pr> --repo
  <checkout>` is the same answer without applying anything: 0 allowed, 7 refused, 3 when the
  box cannot answer.

- The docs say what is enforced: `working-on-this-repo.md` gains both sections and the exit
  codes, `queue-and-prs.md` goes from four rules to six, and its "In this tree" lines now say
  what is on `master` rather than what was in review when the doc was written.

Tests: `tests/test_merge_route.py` commits in a real card worktree through the installed hook
(path, dispatcher marker, operator, amend, an existing trailer, a workspace that cannot name its
card, a stale install) and runs the real `merge_pr.sh` against a fake `ngit` for a PR with no
trailer, one untrailered commit of two, a trailer that names nothing, a running card, a blocked
card, a card named by a commit but not by the link, `Card: operator` against a linked running
card, a PR the bridge has not seen, and the two allowed cases. `ruff check src tests scripts
benchmarks` clean; `pytest -q` 1252 passed.

Card: t_fc8bf1c9

tags: Docs: the two authorship decisions, and why the trailer is not written at merge
git Pull Request: Docs: the two authorship decisions, and why the trailer is not written at merge
events.content:
The rules are in `working-on-this-repo.md` and `queue-and-prs.md`; this is the record of what was
chosen and what was rejected, next to the other decisions in `docs/decisions.md`:

- the trailer is the worker's fact, written by a `commit-msg` hook — not a merge-time
  attribution. A merge can only guess for a PR whose commits never said which card they were
  done under, and rewriting the commits to insert one would change the history the verdict
  covered. An ngit PR lands as `git am`, so the commits are what reach `master`: the trailer
  written once, at commit time, is the one `git log` reads afterwards.
- a merge requires the card in `review` or `done`: `review` is a reviewer's turn, `done` is
  finished, and refusing either would make the rule about a status the merge itself writes.
  `running`, `ready`, `blocked`, `todo`, `scheduled`, `triage` and `archived` are all work that
  has not reached a reviewer.
- the bridge's `ngit_links` row is the PR's card and the trailers are the cards the work was
  done under; both are checked, so `Card: operator` never releases a card the bridge linked.

Card: t_fc8bf1c9
